newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog takes steps to speed up pension review.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog takes steps to speed up pension review.

text.p: The Personal Investment Authority (PIA) said on Friday it had adopted proposals to reduce the amount of information firms need to obtain from occupational pension schemes as part of the pension review process.

The PIA said it had agreed with the assessment by the Securities and Investmnents Board (SIB) that the difficulties faced by reviewing firms in obtaining full sets of information presented a serious obstacle to the completion of the review.
The process was set up in 1994 to investigate the mis-selling of pensions by companies during the late 1980s and early 1990s.
A consultation paper proposing to give effect to SIB guidance designed to speed up redress to people wrongly sold personal pensions was published in November 1996.

The PIA said the difficulties could be overcome or mitigated if the amount of information sought directly from occupational schemes was significantly reduced, other sources of data exploited and standard figures applied where information cannot be obtained.
